evidence_labels: Published findings, local observations, and proposed analyses are identified separately.
hero_title: Enhancers: Exploring the signals that control genes
hero_description: Reproduce published enhancer prediction methods, starting with iEnhancer-2L, then compare their predictions with new experiments. We chose HepG2, K562, and WTC11 because the lentiMPRA study by Agarwal, Inoue et al. (Nature, 2025) tested the same DNA sequences in all three. This lets us ask whether the predictions agree with measured activity in different cells.
hero_alt: A glowing vertical DNA double helix made of binary digits rotates against a dark background. A continuously looping conceptual animation.
visual_caption: Follow the sequence. Evaluate the evidence.
report_notice: Historical report · 10 October 2026. We preserve the initial strategy as a dated record. The current plan reconstructs enhancer predictors, then compares their scores with measurements from Agarwal, Inoue et al. (Nature, 2025). We chose HepG2, K562, and WTC11 because that study tested the same DNA sequences in all three, allowing a matched comparison of predictions and activity. Current references: the updated plan, the four original papers, and the 12 October review. This report’s priorities and counts describe its date, not the current project state.

index: Reproducing original enhancer prediction methods and linking their predictions to new experimental activity data.
research: The replication roadmap, original methods, benchmark limitations, and the bridge to three-cell lentiMPRA.
reproduce: Findings from our iEnhancer-2L reconstruction: the two SVM classifiers, feature comparisons, limitations, and the proposed connection to measured enhancer activity.
publications: Twelve works: four original papers supplied by Prof. Dehzangi and eight newer works, with data links and research roles.
resources: The original benchmark and supplements, plus seven new resource collections; their availability and analysis limits.
notes: Observations, decisions, and open questions as the enhancer research project develops.
strategy: Research report 01: enhancer biology, the collected literature, and an analysis-first research strategy.
methods: Software, original data, setup commands, feature definitions and implementation links for the enhancer-method reconstructions.
mcse: The repaired MCSE-Enhancer benchmark, feature comparisons, and VISTA evaluation plan, preserved as a separate study record.
